# Simply Krisp Produce Guide

> Free, sourced guidance on storing fruits and vegetables so less of them go to waste: where each item belongs (fridge, counter or freezer), how long it lasts, what not to store together, why it spoils, and how to ripen, wash and freeze it. Published by Simply Krisp (https://simplykrisp.com), a produce-freshness company and 1% for the Planet member.

Storage and spoilage facts come mainly from the UC Davis Postharvest Technology Center and USDA sources, and each how-to guide cites its sources inline. Food-safety advice is deliberately conservative. Pages describe quality and common spoilage and are not a substitute for judgment: anything slimy, off-smelling, or moldy on soft produce should be thrown out.

Simply Krisp also sells ethylene absorbers for the crisper drawer. The guides say plainly which produce they help (ethylene-sensitive items) and which they don't.

## Start here

- [Produce Storage Guide](https://guide.simplykrisp.com/): searchable storage guide for 78 fruits and vegetables
- [All produce A to Z](https://guide.simplykrisp.com/produce): every item with storage location and shelf life
- [What went wrong?](https://guide.simplykrisp.com/produce/what-went-wrong): look up a spoilage symptom (mold, sprouting, wilting, browning) and whether to eat, cook, trim or toss
- [How-to guides](https://guide.simplykrisp.com/produce/how-to): ripening, washing, storing leftovers, and fridge vs. counter vs. freezer
- [In season near you](https://guide.simplykrisp.com/seasonal): enter a ZIP code to see which fruits and vegetables are local and in season

## How-to guides

### Ripening

- [How to ripen avocados fast, and how to slow them down](https://guide.simplykrisp.com/produce/how-to/ripen-avocados): Put a hard avocado in a closed bag with an apple or banana to ripen it faster. How to tell when it's ripe, when to refrigerate, and the water hack to skip.
- [How to tell if a mango is ripe, and how to ripen one](https://guide.simplykrisp.com/produce/how-to/is-mango-ripe): Squeeze, don't look: color is not a reliable sign of a ripe mango. How to check ripeness, ripen a hard mango on the counter, and when to refrigerate it.
- [How to ripen bananas faster, or keep them from ripening](https://guide.simplykrisp.com/produce/how-to/ripen-bananas): Bag green bananas with an apple to ripen them faster. To slow ripe bananas, refrigerate them: the peel darkens but the fruit stays good for a few more days.
- [How to ripen kiwi, and keep ripe kiwi from going mushy](https://guide.simplykrisp.com/produce/how-to/ripen-kiwi): Ripen firm kiwi on the counter in 2 to 3 days, or faster in a bag with an apple or banana. Then refrigerate it, away from apples, so it doesn't go mushy.
- [How to ripen pears, and how to tell when they're ready](https://guide.simplykrisp.com/produce/how-to/ripen-pears): Pears ripen on the counter, not the tree. Speed them up in a paper bag with an apple or banana, check the neck daily, then refrigerate ripe pears.

### Washing

- [How to wash strawberries and other berries, and whether vinegar helps](https://guide.simplykrisp.com/produce/how-to/wash-strawberries): Wash strawberries right before eating, under cool running water, then pat them dry. What the FDA says about soap and produce washes, and what a vinegar soak does.
- [How to wash grapes](https://guide.simplykrisp.com/produce/how-to/wash-grapes): Rinse grapes under cool running water right before eating and pat them dry. The white powdery film is bloom, a natural coating, not pesticide. No soap needed.
- [How to wash vegetables and lettuce](https://guide.simplykrisp.com/produce/how-to/wash-vegetables): Rinse vegetables under cool running water, scrub firm ones with a brush, and soak leafy greens. When to skip washing, and why soap and produce washes aren't needed.

### Storing leftovers

- [How to store a cut onion](https://guide.simplykrisp.com/produce/how-to/store-cut-onion): Store a cut or half onion in a sealed container in the fridge and use it within about 7 days. Cut onions aren't poisonous. How to freeze chopped onion.
- [How to store pomegranate seeds](https://guide.simplykrisp.com/produce/how-to/store-pomegranate-seeds): Store pomegranate seeds in an airtight container in the fridge and eat them within a few days to a week, or freeze them on a tray. How to get the seeds out cleanly.
- [How to store a cut avocado](https://guide.simplykrisp.com/produce/how-to/store-cut-avocado): Squeeze lemon or lime juice on cut avocado, wrap it tightly with no air, and refrigerate. Why it browns, how to store guacamole, and why not to store it in water.
- [How to store peeled garlic](https://guide.simplykrisp.com/produce/how-to/store-peeled-garlic): Refrigerate peeled garlic cloves in a covered container and use them within about a week, or freeze them. Why homemade garlic in oil needs special care.

### Fridge, counter and freezer

- [Fridge or counter? Where every fruit and vegetable goes](https://guide.simplykrisp.com/produce/how-to/fridge-or-counter): Which fruits and vegetables go in the fridge, which stay on the counter, which ripen first, and which belong in the pantry. A full list for 78 kinds of produce.
- [Can you freeze it? A freezing chart for fruits and vegetables](https://guide.simplykrisp.com/produce/how-to/can-you-freeze-it): Which fruits and vegetables freeze well, which need blanching first, and which don't freeze well at all, like lettuce and cucumbers. Blanching times included.
- [How to organize your fridge so produce lasts longer](https://guide.simplykrisp.com/produce/how-to/organize-fridge): Keep the fridge at 40°F or below, put things that wilt in the high-humidity drawer and things that rot in the low-humidity drawer, and keep apples away from greens.
